summary.en: The present simple tense is used to describe habits, unchanging situations, general truths, and fixed arrangements.
summary.fa: زمان حال ساده برای توصیف عادات، وضعیت‌های ثابت، حقایق عمومی و ترتیبات ثابت استفاده می‌شود.

en: Use base form of verb for I, you, we, they
Add -s/-es to verb for he, she, it
Use "do/does" for questions and negatives
Regular habits use present simple (e.g., "I wake up at 7 AM")
fa: از شکل پایه فعل برای I، you، we، they استفاده کنید
به فعل برای he، she، it -s/-es اضافه کنید
برای سوالات و جملات منفی از "do/does" استفاده کنید
عادات معمولی از زمان حال ساده استفاده می‌کنند (مثلاً "I wake up at 7 AM")

en: I work in a bank. (fact)
She plays tennis every weekend. (habit)
Water boils at 100°C. (general truth)
The train leaves at 9:00 AM. (fixed arrangement)
fa: من در یک بانک کار می‌کنم. (واقعیت)
او هر آخر هفته تنیس بازی می‌کند. (عادت)
آب در 100 درجه سانتی‌گراد می‌جوشد. (حقیقت عمومی)
قطار در ساعت 9:00 صبح حرکت می‌کند. (ترتیب ثابت)

en.explanation: Third person singular (he, she, it) requires -s/-es ending
With auxiliary "does", use base form of the verb

fa.wrong: He go to school every day.
fa.correct: He goes to school every day.
fa.explanation: در سوم شخص مفرد (he/she/it) باید به فعل -s یا -es اضافه شود.
بعد از "does" باید شکل پایه فعل بیاید و -s حذف شود.

en.question: She ___ (go) to the gym every day.
en.explanation: Third person singular (she) requires -es ending

en.question: They ___ (not/like) coffee.
en.explanation: Use "don't" with plural subjects (they)

fa.question: جای خالی را پر کنید: She ___ to the gym every day.
fa.explanation: برای سوم شخص مفرد (she) باید -s/-es اضافه شود.

fa.question: کدام گزینه درست است؟ They ___ coffee.
fa.explanation: برای فاعل جمع (they) از "don't" استفاده می‌شود.

summary.en: Articles come before nouns. Use a/an for general things and the for specific ones.
summary.fa: حروف تعریف قبل از اسم می‌آیند؛ برای چیزهای کلی از a/an و برای چیزهای مشخص از the استفاده می‌شود.

en: Use a before consonant sounds
Use an before vowel sounds
Use the when both speaker and listener know the noun
Do not use a/an with plural nouns
Do not use a/an with uncountable nouns
fa: قبل از صدای همخوان از a استفاده کنید
قبل از صدای واکه از an استفاده کنید
وقتی اسم مشخص است از the استفاده کنید
با اسم‌های جمع از a/an استفاده نمی‌شود
با اسم‌های غیرقابل شمارش از a/an استفاده نمی‌شود

en: I have a book. (general)
She eats an apple. (vowel sound)
The book is on the table. (specific)
We need water. (uncountable)
fa: من یک کتاب دارم. (کلی)
او یک سیب می‌خورد. (صدای واکه)
کتاب روی میز است. (مشخص)
ما به آب نیاز داریم. (غیرقابل شمارش)

en.explanation: Use a/an with singular countable nouns.
Use a before consonant sounds like /b/.

fa.explanation: با اسم مفرد قابل شمارش باید a/an بیاید.
قبل از صدای همخوان مثل /b/ از a استفاده می‌شود.

en.question: She has ___ umbrella.
en.explanation: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound.

en.question: ___ sun is bright today.
en.explanation: The sun is specific and unique.

fa.question: She has ___ umbrella.
fa.explanation: Umbrella با صدای واکه شروع می‌شود.

fa.question: ___ sun is bright today.
fa.explanation: خورشید مشخص و یکتا است؛ the لازم است.

summary.en: Use demonstratives to point to people or things near or far, singular or plural.
summary.fa: برای اشاره به افراد یا اشیای نزدیک/دور و مفرد/جمع از اشاره‌گرها استفاده می‌شود.

en: This = near + singular
That = far + singular
These = near + plural
Those = far + plural
Demonstratives come before nouns
fa: This = نزدیک + مفرد
That = دور + مفرد
These = نزدیک + جمع
Those = دور + جمع
اشاره‌گرها قبل از اسم می‌آیند

en: This book is interesting. (near)
That car is fast. (far)
These apples are fresh. (near plural)
Those shoes are expensive. (far plural)
fa: این کتاب جالب است. (نزدیک)
آن ماشین سریع است. (دور)
این سیب‌ها تازه‌اند. (جمع نزدیک)
آن کفش‌ها گران هستند. (جمع دور)

en.explanation: Use these with plural nouns.
Use that with singular nouns.

fa.explanation: برای اسم جمع از these استفاده می‌شود.
برای اسم مفرد از that استفاده می‌شود.

en.question: ___ is my phone here. (near, singular)
en.explanation: This is used for near, singular.

en.question: ___ houses are big. (far, plural)
en.explanation: Those is used for far, plural.

fa.question: ___ is my phone here. (near, singular)
fa.explanation: برای نزدیک و مفرد از this استفاده می‌شود.

fa.question: ___ houses are big. (far, plural)
fa.explanation: برای دور و جمع از those استفاده می‌شود.

fa: ملکی

summary.en: Possessive adjectives show ownership and come before nouns.
summary.fa: صفت‌های ملکی مالکیت را نشان می‌دهند و قبل از اسم می‌آیند.

en: Use my, your, his, her, its, our, their
Place them before the noun
Do not use articles with possessive adjectives
Its is for things/animals; their is for plural
Possessive adjectives do not change for plural nouns
fa: از my, your, his, her, its, our, their استفاده کنید
این صفت‌ها قبل از اسم می‌آیند
با صفت ملکی از a/an/the استفاده نکنید
Its برای اشیا/حیوانات و their برای جمع است
صفت‌های ملکی با جمع شدن اسم تغییر نمی‌کنند

en: This is my book. (ownership)
Her bag is red. (her)
Our class starts at 9. (our)
Their house is big. (their)
fa: این کتاب من است. (مالکیت)
کیف او قرمز است. (her)
کلاس ما ساعت ۹ شروع می‌شود. (our)
خانه آنها بزرگ است. (their)

en.explanation: Do not use the with possessive adjectives.
Possessive adjectives go directly before nouns.

fa.explanation: با صفت ملکی the استفاده نمی‌شود.
صفت ملکی باید درست قبل از اسم بیاید.

en.question: We love ___ teacher.
en.explanation: Our is the possessive adjective.

en.question: ___ phone is new. (belonging to him)
en.explanation: His shows ownership for he.

fa.question: We love ___ teacher.
fa.explanation: Our صفت ملکی است.

fa.question: ___ phone is new. (belonging to him)
fa.explanation: His مالکیت را برای he نشان می‌دهد.

summary.en: Imperatives are used to give commands, instructions, or requests.
summary.fa: امری‌ها برای دستور دادن، راهنما دادن یا درخواست استفاده می‌شوند.

en: Use the base verb without a subject
Add please to make it polite
Negative imperative: Do not + base verb
Use it for instructions and directions
You is understood, not written
fa: از شکل پایه فعل بدون فاعل استفاده کنید
برای مؤدبانه شدن از please استفاده کنید
امری منفی: Do not + فعل پایه
برای دستور و راهنما استفاده می‌شود
فاعل you به طور ضمنی وجود دارد

en: Open the door. (command)
Please sit down. (polite)
Do not touch that. (negative)
Turn left at the corner. (instruction)
fa: در را باز کن. (دستور)
لطفاً بنشین. (مودبانه)
به آن دست نزن. (منفی)
سرِ چهارراه به چپ بپیچ. (راهنما)

en.explanation: Imperatives do not use a subject.
After don't, use the base verb.

fa.explanation: در امری فاعل نوشته نمی‌شود.
بعد از don't از فعل پایه استفاده می‌شود.

en.question: Choose the imperative sentence.
en.explanation: Imperatives use the base verb without subject.

en.question: Negative imperative:
en.explanation: Use Don't + base verb.

fa.question: کدام جمله امری است؟
fa.explanation: امری با فعل پایه و بدون فاعل می‌آید.

fa.question: امری منفی کدام است؟
fa.explanation: ساختار درست: Don't + فعل پایه.

summary.en: Use in, on, and at to talk about time and place in simple sentences.
summary.fa: برای زمان و مکان در جملات ساده از in، on و at استفاده می‌شود.

en: In for months, years, and long periods
On for days and dates
At for specific times
In for enclosed places (in a room)
On for surfaces; at for points (at the door)
fa: in برای ماه‌ها، سال‌ها و دوره‌های طولانی
on برای روزها و تاریخ‌ها
at برای زمان مشخص
in برای مکان‌های بسته (in a room)
on برای سطح و at برای نقطه (at the door)

en: We meet at 7 o'clock. (time)
She was born in 2010. (year)
The class is on Monday. (day)
The keys are on the table. (surface)
fa: ما ساعت ۷ ملاقات می‌کنیم. (زمان)
او در سال ۲۰۱۰ به دنیا آمد. (سال)
کلاس روز دوشنبه است. (روز)
کلیدها روی میز هستند. (سطح)

en.explanation: Use at for specific times.
Use in for years.

fa.explanation: برای زمان مشخص از at استفاده می‌شود.
برای سال از in استفاده می‌شود.

en.question: Choose the correct preposition: I work ___ Monday.
en.explanation: Use on with days.

en.question: Choose the correct preposition: The meeting is ___ 3 PM.
en.explanation: Use at with specific times.

fa.question: حرف اضافه درست را انتخاب کنید: I work ___ Monday.
fa.explanation: برای روز از on استفاده می‌شود.

fa.question: حرف اضافه درست را انتخاب کنید: The meeting is ___ 3 PM.
fa.explanation: برای زمان مشخص از at استفاده می‌شود.

sections.summary: The present continuous (progressive) tense describes actions happening now or temporary situations.
rules: Form: subject + am/is/are + verb-ing
Use for actions happening right now
Use for temporary situations
Use for future arrangements with time expressions
examples: I am studying English now. (action happening now)
She is living in Paris this year. (temporary situation)
They are meeting tomorrow at 3 PM. (future arrangement)
It is raining outside. (happening now)

commonMistakes.explanation: Stative verbs (know, like, want) are not normally used in continuous form
Must use am/is/are before the -ing form

quiz.question: Look! It ___ (rain).
quiz.explanation: Use present continuous for actions happening right now

quiz.question: We ___ (have) dinner tomorrow at 7 PM.
quiz.explanation: Present continuous can express future arrangements

sections.summary: The past simple tense is used to describe completed actions in the past.
rules: Regular verbs: add -ed to base form
Irregular verbs: use specific past form
Use "did" for questions and negatives
Time expressions: yesterday, last week, ago, in 2010
examples: I visited London last year. (completed action)
She studied French for five years. (completed duration)
They didn't come to the party. (negative)
Did you see that movie? (question)

commonMistakes.explanation: After "did/didn't", use base form of verb
Go is irregular; past form is "went", not "goed"

quiz.question: She ___ (buy) a new car last month.
quiz.explanation: Buy is irregular; past form is "bought"

quiz.question: Did you ___ (see) John yesterday?
quiz.explanation: After "did", use base form of verb

summary.en: Words have different jobs in a sentence, such as naming things, showing actions, or describing.

افعال عمل یا حالت را نشان می‌دهند

Use an article before a singular countable noun.

قبل از اسم مفرد قابل شمارش از a/an استفاده می‌شود.

en.question: Which word is an adjective? The small house is blue.
en.explanation: Small describes the noun house.

fa.question: اسم را انتخاب کنید: The cat sleeps.

fa.question: کدام کلمه صفت است؟ The small house is blue.

summary.en: Basic English sentences often follow Subject + Verb + Object order.
summary.fa: جملات ساده انگلیسی معمولاً ترتیب فاعل + فعل + مفعول دارند.

en: Subject tells who or what the sentence is about
Verb shows the action or state
Object receives the action
English word order is usually S + V + O
Time/place can come at the end
fa: فاعل نشان می‌دهد درباره چه کسی یا چه چیزی است
فعل عمل یا حالت را نشان می‌دهد
مفعول عمل را دریافت می‌کند

زمان/مکان معمولاً در پایان می‌آید

en: Sara eats an apple. (S+V+O)
They play football. (S+V+O)
I read books at night. (time at end)
The teacher explains the lesson. (S+V+O)
fa: سارا یک سیب می‌خورد. (فاعل+فعل+مفعول)
آنها فوتبال بازی می‌کنند. (فاعل+فعل+مفعول)

معلم درس را توضیح می‌دهد. (فاعل+فعل+مفعول)

en.explanation: English sentences usually start with the subject.
Keep the verb after the subject in basic sentences.

fa.explanation: در انگلیسی معمولاً جمله با فاعل شروع می‌شود.
در جملات ساده، فعل بعد از فاعل می‌آید.

en.question: Choose the correct order: (eat / I / breakfast).

en.question: Which word is the subject? "The boy kicks the ball."

fa.question: ترتیب درست را انتخاب کنید: (eat / I / breakfast).

fa.question: در جمله "The boy kicks the ball" فاعل کدام است؟

en: Start a sentence with a capital letter
Use a period for statements
Use a question mark for questions

برای جدا کردن موارد در فهرست از ویرگول استفاده کنید

Do you like tea? (question mark)

در گفتار از شکل کوتاه استفاده می‌شود: I'm, he's, they're

summary.en: Can shows ability in the present. Could is used for past ability or polite requests. Both are easy ways to speak politely and clearly.
summary.fa: Can توانایی در حال را نشان می‌دهد. Could برای توانایی گذشته یا درخواست مودبانه است. این دو فعل مدال کاربرد زیادی دارند.

en: Use can for present ability (I can swim).
Use could for past ability (She could read at five).
Use can for simple requests (Can you help me?).
Use could for polite requests (Could you open the door?).
Modal verbs use base verb (He can speak English).
Negatives use cannot/can't (I can't come today).
Questions use can/could first (Can they wait?).
fa: برای توانایی حال از can استفاده کنید (I can swim).
برای توانایی گذشته از could استفاده کنید (She could read at five).
برای درخواست ساده از can استفاده کنید (Can you help me?).
برای درخواست مودبانه از could استفاده کنید (Could you open the door?).
بعد از مدال فعل پایه می‌آید (He can speak English).
منفی با cannot/can't است (I can't come today).
در سوال، can/could اول می‌آید (Can they wait?).

en: I can drive. (ability)
She can cook well. (ability)
He could run fast as a child. (past ability)

Can you pass the salt? (request)
Could you repeat that? (polite request)
They can't come today. (negative)
Could I sit here? (polite request)
fa: من می‌توانم رانندگی کنم. (توانایی)

او در کودکی می‌توانست سریع بدود. (گذشته)

می‌توانی نمک را بدهی؟ (درخواست)
ممکن است دوباره تکرار کنید؟ (مودبانه)
آنها امروز نمی‌توانند بیایند. (منفی)
می‌توانم اینجا بنشینم؟ (مودبانه)

en.explanation: Use the base verb after can/could.
Do not use to after modal verbs.
Negatives still use the base verb.

fa.explanation: بعد از can/could فعل پایه می‌آید.
بعد از فعل مدال to نمی‌آید.

summary.en: Going to is used for future plans and intentions. It is also used for predictions with clear evidence. It is common in everyday speech.
summary.fa: Going to برای برنامه‌ها و قصدهای آینده استفاده می‌شود. همچنین برای پیش‌بینی با شواهد واضح به کار می‌رود. در گفتار روزمره رایج است.

en: Form: am/is/are + going to + base verb (I am going to study).
Use for plans (She is going to visit her aunt).
Use for intentions (We are going to start early).
Use for evidence-based predictions (Look at the sky, it is going to rain).
Negatives: am/is/are not going to (He isn't going to come).
Questions: Am/Is/Are + subject + going to (Are you going to travel?).
fa: ساختار: am/is/are + going to + فعل پایه (I am going to study).
برای برنامه از آن استفاده کنید (She is going to visit her aunt).
برای قصد استفاده کنید (We are going to start early).
برای پیش‌بینی با شاهد استفاده کنید (Look at the sky, it is going to rain).
منفی: am/is/are not going to (He isn't going to come).
سوالی: Am/Is/Are + فاعل + going to (Are you going to travel?).

Use the base verb after going to.

summary.en: Will is used for quick decisions and predictions. It is common in promises and offers too. It does not show a fixed plan like going to.

en: Form: will + base verb (I will call you).
Use for predictions (It will snow tomorrow).
Use for quick decisions (I will answer the phone).
Use for promises (I will help you).
Use for offers (I will carry the bag).
Negatives: will not / won't (She won't come).

برای پیش‌بینی استفاده می‌شود (It will snow tomorrow).
برای تصمیم سریع استفاده می‌شود (I will answer the phone).
برای قول دادن می‌آید (I will help you).
برای پیشنهاد می‌آید (I will carry the bag).
منفی: will not / won't (She won't come).

After will, use the base form.

بعد از will فعل پایه استفاده می‌شود.

en: Form: am/is/are + verb-ing (I am working).
Negative: am/is/are + not + verb-ing (She isn't sleeping).
Question: Am/Is/Are + subject + verb-ing? (Are you studying?).
Use for 'now/at the moment/today/this week'.
Spelling: drop final -e (make→making), double consonant (run→running).
Not for permanent facts (use present simple for facts).

summary.en: Use the present continuous (be + verb-ing) for actions happening now or around now, and for planned near-future arrangements.

en: Form: am/is/are + verb-ing (I am working).
Negative: am/is/are + not + verb-ing (She isn't sleeping).
Question: Am/Is/Are + subject + verb-ing? (Are you studying?).
Use for 'now/at the moment/today/this week'.
Spelling: drop final -e (make→making), double consonant (run→running).
Not for permanent facts (use present simple for facts).
fa: Form: am/is/are + verb-ing (I am working).

Question: Am/Is/Are + subject + verb-ing? (Are you studying?).
Use for 'now/at the moment/today/this week'.
Spelling: drop final -e (make→making), double consonant (run→running).
Not for permanent facts (use present simple for facts).

en: I am studying now. (now)
She is cooking at the moment. (now)

He is meeting the doctor tomorrow. (arrangement)
The kids are playing outside. (now)
I'm not feeling well today. (temporary state)

summary.en: Zero conditional talks about general truths and habits. Use present simple in both clauses.

en: Form: If + present simple, present simple (If you heat ice, it melts).
Use for facts/science rules (If water boils, it turns to steam).
Use for habits/results (If I am late, I call).
If-clause can come first or second (Ice melts if you heat it).
Use comma when if-clause comes first.
Do not use will in zero conditional results.

Use comma when if-clause comes first.

en: If you heat ice, it melts.
If it rains, the ground gets wet.
If I don't sleep, I feel tired.
If you mix red and blue, you get purple.
Plants die if they don't get water.
If you press this button, the light turns on.
If he eats too fast, he feels sick.
I take an umbrella if it rains.

summary.en: First conditional talks about real, possible future situations. Use present simple in the if-clause and will/can/may in the main clause.
summary.fa: First conditional talks about real, possible future situations. Use present simple in the if-clause and will/can/may in the main clause.

en: Form: If + present simple, will + base verb (If it rains, I'll stay home).
Use for possible future results, not general truths.
If-clause can come first or second; comma when first.
Use can/may instead of will for ability/permission (If I finish, I can go).
Don't use will in the if-clause (not: If it will rain...).
Use unless = if not (Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus).

Don't use will in the if-clause (not: If it will rain...).
Use unless = if not (Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus).

en: If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.

If they invite us, we'll go.
If you don't feel well, you should rest.

en: Form: If + past simple, would + base verb (If I had time, I would travel).
Use for imaginary or unlikely situations now/future.
Use 'were' for all subjects in formal style (If I were you...).
Result can use could/might (If I had money, I could buy it).
If-clause can come first or second; comma when first.
Not about past facts; it's about hypothetical present/future.

en: Form: If + past perfect, would have + past participle (If I had studied, I would have passed).
Use for past regrets and imagined different past results.
You can use could have/might have for ability/possibility.
If-clause can come first or second; comma when first.
Do not mix with present meaning unless you intend mixed conditionals.
Past perfect: had + past participle.

sections.summary: Articles are words that define nouns as specific or unspecific. English has two types: definite (the) and indefinite (a/an).
rules: Use "a" before consonant sounds
Use "an" before vowel sounds
Use "the" for specific nouns or when something is mentioned again
No article for plural/uncountable nouns in general statements
examples: I saw a dog. The dog was brown. (first mention → specific)
She is an engineer. (job/profession)
The sun rises in the east. (unique things)
I like coffee. (general - no article with uncountable)

commonMistakes.explanation: Student starts with consonant sound /st/, use "a"
No article when referring to the general purpose (education)

quiz.question: She is ___ honest person.
quiz.explanation: Honest starts with vowel sound /ɒ/, use "an"

quiz.question: I love ___ music.
quiz.explanation: General statements with uncountable nouns need no article

sections.summary: Prepositions show relationships between nouns and other words. The most common are in, on, at.
rules: Time: at (specific times), on (days/dates), in (months/years/periods)
Place: at (specific points), on (surfaces), in (enclosed spaces)
at: at 3 PM, at night, at home, at the door
on: on Monday, on the table, on the wall
in: in May, in 2020, in the morning, in the room
examples: I wake up at 7 AM. (specific time)
The meeting is on Monday. (day)
She was born in 1990. (year)
The book is on the table. (surface)
He lives in New York. (city/enclosed space)

commonMistakes.wrong: I will see you in Monday.
commonMistakes.correct: I will see you on Monday.
commonMistakes.explanation: Use "on" with days of the week

commonMistakes.wrong: The class starts at the morning.
commonMistakes.correct: The class starts in the morning.
commonMistakes.explanation: Use "in" with parts of the day (except "at night")

quiz.question: The party is ___ Saturday night.
quiz.explanation: Use "on" with specific days and nights of the week

sections.summary: Modal verbs express ability, permission, obligation, advice, or possibility.
rules: Can/could: ability, permission, possibility
Should/ought to: advice, recommendation
Must/have to: obligation, necessity
May/might: permission, possibility
Modal + base form (no "to" except ought to)
examples: I can swim. (ability)
You should see a doctor. (advice)
We must arrive on time. (obligation)
It might rain tomorrow. (possibility)

commonMistakes.explanation: Modal verbs are followed by base form without "to"
Modal verbs don't add -s in third person

sections.summary: Conditional sentences express hypothetical situations and their consequences.
rules: Zero conditional: If + present, present (general truths)
First conditional: If + present, will + base (real future possibility)
Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base (unreal present)
Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle (unreal past)
examples: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils. (zero - scientific fact)
If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home. (first - possible future)
If I had a million dollars, I would travel the world. (second - unreal present)
If I had studied harder, I would have passed. (third - unreal past)

commonMistakes.wrong: If I will see him, I will tell him.
commonMistakes.correct: If I see him, I will tell him.
commonMistakes.explanation: First conditional: use present simple in if-clause, not "will"

commonMistakes.wrong: If I would be rich, I would buy a house.
commonMistakes.correct: If I were rich, I would buy a house.
commonMistakes.explanation: Second conditional: use past simple in if-clause, not "would"

quiz.question: If she ___ (study) harder, she will pass the exam.
quiz.explanation: First conditional: present simple in if-clause

quiz.question: If I ___ (be) you, I would apologize.
quiz.explanation: Second conditional: use "were" for all persons in formal English

sections.summary: The passive voice emphasizes the action or receiver rather than the doer.
rules: Form: be + past participle
Use when doer is unknown, unimportant, or obvious
Can be used in all tenses
Add "by" to mention the doer (if necessary)
examples: The car was stolen last night. (doer unknown)
English is spoken in many countries. (doer obvious)
The letter will be sent tomorrow. (focus on action)
The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci. (famous doer mentioned)

commonMistakes.explanation: Use past participle (written), not past simple (wrote)

commonMistakes.correct: The house is being built now.
commonMistakes.explanation: Present continuous passive: is/are being + past participle

quiz.question: A new hospital ___ (build) in our town next year.
quiz.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle
